security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG multi-hart emulation, when a guest hart H enters a constrained LR/SC loop, QEMU must guarantee forward progress via one of: (a) successful SC by any hart on H's reservation set, (b) unconditional store/AMO from another hart/device on the reservation set, (c) H branching out of the loop, or (d) H trapping. This guarantee is violated if QEMU's reservation tracking state for H is spuriously cleared without any of the above events occurring—for example, if the per-hart load reservation is lost on an unrelated CSR write, on an exception entry/return that incorrectly resets reservation state, or if TCG register allocation causes the reservation monitor to be silently invalidated without architected side-effects completing.
security_spec.summary: Splitting norm:constrained_lrsc_forward_progress into five granular sub-tags (intro, sc, store_amo, branch, trap) clarifies that QEMU must not spuriously invalidate LR reservations—any reservation loss without an architected store, successful SC, branch exit, or trap constitutes a forward-progress denial-of-service against the guest hart's constrained LR/SC loop

findings.finding: LR correctly loads data into load_val (via tcg_gen_qemu_ld_tl) and stores the reservation address into load_res (via tcg_gen_mov_tl). Both are TCG globals backed by per-vCPU CPURISCVState fields, so multi-hart isolation is maintained. Memory barriers for .aq/.rl/.ztso are correctly emitted.

SC correctly compares load_res with the store address, then uses tcg_gen_atomic_cmpxchg_tl(addr=load_res, cmp=load_val, new=src2). On address mismatch, probes write permissions and sets rd=1. Reservation is unconditionally cleared (load_res = -1) after both success and failure paths, which is spec-correct: any SC clears the reservation. No spurious clearing within the LR/SC pair in single-hart execution.

Reservation is cleared on every privilege mode transition (exception entry, MRET/SRET/MNRET, gdbstub priv write). The comment explicitly documents this as spec-compliant: ISA v2.2 required it, later revisions say the kernel 'should' use SC to yield. This is a conservative, defensive implementation that prevents cross-context reservation leaks. No spurious clearing in normal execution.

WRS.STO correctly clears the load reservation at translate time (tcg_gen_movi_tl(load_res, -1)) before exiting the TB. Per the Zawrs spec, the WRS instruction sequence must cause any pending LR reservation to be lost.

WRS.NTO calls gen_helper_wrs_nto which may raise an exception. When an exception fires, riscv_raise_exception causes a longjmp into riscv_cpu_do_interrupt, which calls riscv_cpu_set_mode, which clears load_res at cpu_helper.c:1105. When no exception fires, falls through to trans_wrs_sto which also clears load_res. Both paths correctly clear the reservation.
Both load_res and load_val are included in the VMState via VMSTATE_UINTTL at lines 437-438. Reservation state is correctly migrated, preventing silent corruption on live migration.
Reset correctly initializes load_res = -1 (no reservation). Correct behavior per spec.
load_res and load_val are registered as TCG global registers backed by CPURISCVState fields. Each vCPU has its own TCG context with its own globals. No cross-hart leakage of reservation state.

SC uses load_res (the reservation address) as the addr parameter to tcg_gen_atomic_cmpxchg_tl and load_val (the loaded data) as the cmp (expected old value). This is correct. However, QEMU TCG does NOT implement cross-hart reservation invalidation: a store/AMO from hart B to hart A's reservation set does NOT clear hart A's load_res. This is a known limitation of QEMU's simplified per-hart reservation model. The RISC-V spec requires SC to fail if another hart stores to the reservation set. This could violate the forward-progress guarantee in constrained LR/SC loops under multi-hart TCG emulation.
